Installer note, I have an HE3 that was purchased late 2003. There are Torx screws as well as standard phillips screws. Just remove the 6 phillip screws to remove the front of the door (the plastic front housing) and there are 2 screws inside that hold the handle on. Two screws on the bottom of the door, one on either side (the middle of the 3 screws on each side) and one on each side on the top of the door. Install takes 10 minutes.

Replacing the broken items in my refrigerator was not straight forward but I got it done. If you have a broken shelf clip like this, here's how I replaced mine:
1. Use a tiny drill bit and drill a hole about 1/4" deep into the round peg that will be flush on an installed clip
2. Screw a screw part way into that tiny hole drilled in step 1
3. Use a pair of pliers and pull outward on the screw to pull the round peg out. Note that it may come all the way out or it may not
4. Once you have the peg out or out as far as it will go, pull the rest of the broken clip out. If the clip remains tight to the refrigerator case, use a plastic putty knife and work it around the clip to work it out
5. Place the new clip in place and use a hammer to hammer the round peg flush with the clip.

You may end up with 2 tiny barbs broken off in the refrigerator case. Use a small nail to drive them into the case and off to the side.

The support uses an expansion fitting with a pin you drive into the expansion fitting to secure it to the inside of the refrigerator wall. When I attempted to install the replacement part, the extra material on the pin (see picture) made it impossible to drive into the expansion fitting, and almost broke the new support. Thankfully, I salvaged the pin from the old failed support, and used that to secure it to the wall.

Some people might lose their old pin inside the wall of the refrigerator, so I would recommend a different slightly more expensive version with better quality control.

Update: Added a picture of the pin that keeps this piece from functioning at all. The pin should be smooth from the shaft to the point, but this one had a bunch of chaff and extra material that would require nipping or grinding/shaving off to use. It isn't just a little piece, either, but thick, as though it were cast that way.
